key_insight: Longer calendar lookback improved colorectal cancer prediction modestly, with about 80% of the AUROC gain reached by 10 years and a plateau around 18 years.
clinical_relevance: Historical primary-care records may add predictive signal, but modest discrimination does not establish clinical screening utility.
method: Pretrained a 34.6M-parameter transformer on 1.4B coded events from 3.6M patients.
Fine-tuned for incident colorectal cancer prediction with a 12-month pre-diagnostic buffer.
Compared 15 lookback windows spanning 2–30 years in the same patients, alongside XGBoost.
evidence_signal: In 1,008 cases and 9,582 matched controls registered for at least 30 years, transformer AUROC rose from 0.551 at 2 years to 0.590 at 18 years; XGBoost peaked at 0.589.
watch_item: Results from long-registered patients in one region may not generalize to populations with shorter or fragmented EHR histories.
paper_title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
